why_this_matters_more_than_a_between_arm: The design varies the reasoning budget and reads accuracy against it. But the budget ALSO determines how many rows are measurable at all: at cap150 none of deepseek's rows are measurable, at cap400 12 are, at cap1000 21 are. So the independent variable moved the dependent variable's denominator, which means the monotone rise 0.000 -> 0.083 -> 0.271 is not evidence about a sweet spot -- it is arithmetically what an unmeasurable-to-measurable shift looks like. The published pooled_p=0.003906 is therefore not interpretable for the deepseek arm.
do_not_overcorrect: This does NOT establish that deepseek-r1:7b is better than qwen2.5:7b. rate_on_measurable_rows is conditioned on the model producing an answer under that budget, and that condition is itself the thing being varied -- it is a selection on the outcome. What is now established: (a) cap150's 0.000 must not be cited as a measured zero, it is an absent measurement in the same sense coderepair-01's llama3.2:3b cells were; (b) cap400/cap1000 published rates understate their measurable-subset rates by 0.250 and 0.348; (c) any claim about an optimal budget needs availability and accuracy reported as two separate columns, never folded into one rate.
knowable_without_data: partly yes. The mechanism was already written down twice before this run: the workspace note 免费API通道2026-10-07.md says 'inference models: content can come back empty, take the content field, avoid', and shared/ollama_guard.py documents the 0-char rejection it uses. What was NOT knowable in advance is the per-cap distribution -- that only the 100+ item measurement reveals.
collector_gap_relative_to_the_sibling: CORRECTED after checking rather than assuming: run_sweetspot_amp.py DOES have the coderepair preflight -- it imports resolve_models from run_coderepair, which drops tags ollama does not have before any measurement, and result.json records models_requested == models_measured == ['qwen2.5:7b','deepseek-r1:7b'], so nothing was dropped and absent models are NOT what happened here. The real gap is narrower and worse: this collector already has an availability column, `truncated`, built on the right principle ('truncation at the cap is an infrastructure event, not a model failure ... a cap effect is never manufactured out of our own budget setting') -- but it recognises only the TRUNCATED reason. It records 0 for every cap here, while 111 deepseek-r1 rows died as 'ollama returned error-text (0 chars)' and fell into the generic exception bucket, where acc = passed / len(items) charges them to capability. So the accounting that should have caught this existed, was pointed at the right idea, and had too narrow a predicate.
recommended_reporting_shape: Every future arm rate should carry three numbers, not one: measured_rate over measurable rows, availability = measurable/total, and the raw counts. lineage-01 needed exactly this split and had to be reconstructed by hand (v3c: 0.7778 on what it answered, 8/50 it never answered, net 0.6533).
